title: SLO-tightening regression during cross-region surge — staggered circuit-breaker lockstep and load-shed remediation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: On 2026-03-05 a cross-region traffic surge triggered near-simultaneous circuit-breaker trips in US-West1 and EU-West1. A recent SLO threshold tightening rollout coupled with a config propagation bug caused effectively identical hysteresis and token-bucket state across regions. This produced lockstep circuit-breaker behavior, large-scale shedding of priority queues, and a sustained SLO miss for p99 latency over a 27-minute window. The incident affected hosted inference endpoints and a subset of Dedicated customers routed through regional affinity policies.
timeline:

root_cause: Two coincident factors: 1) A SLO-threshold tightening config (tighten-slo-2026-03) was staged via the rollout service and accidentally promoted to production without canary gating. 2) A bug in the rollout agent caused config propagation to be synchronous and identical across regions for hysteresis and token-bucket seeds, removing intended per-region jitter. This allowed a traffic surge to push both regions past identical trip points, producing lockstep CB trips and amplified failover load.
detection_and_alerting: Detection relied on standard SLO-based alerts (p99 latency) and per-region circuit-breaker telemetry. Gaps: missing synthetic checks probing tail latency under low-probability fanout conditions, and no alert that detected synchronous CB trips across regions. Alert throttling also delayed paging to on-call for 3 minutes due to a suppression rule during a related deployment window.
impact: Duration: ~27 minutes of elevated p99 latency. Affected: 14% of live hosted routes saw degraded tail latency; 3 Dedicated customers experienced degraded throughput due to priority-shed. Business impact: increased error budget consumption and a small number of support escalations. No customer data loss.
short_term_mitigation: 1) Immediate rollback of tighten-slo-2026-03 to previous thresholds. 2) Manually reset circuit-breaker state and token-bucket counters in affected regions. 3) Throttled failover routing to avoid amplifying fanout. 4) Temporarily disabled synchronous propagation in rollout agent.
long_term_mitigation: 1) Enforce canary gating for SLO/config changes: at least one region with synthetic tail-latency checks before global promotion. 2) Introduce per-region random jitter for CB hysteresis and token-bucket seeds; default jitter range 5-12%. 3) Add cross-region correlation alert that fires if two or more CBs trip within a 60s window for the same route. 4) Implement per-region token-bucket capacity and burst isolation to avoid shared exhaustion. 5) Update rollout agent to ensure eventual consistency with region-specific overrides and a safe promotion path.
